correctness.rationale: For n>=7 the graph has four distinct generators. The binary indicator satisfies an explicit eigenvalue equation with integer mean b/(4-a+b). Its nonzero Fourier modes must be cyclotomic zeros of a degree-six polynomial; exact integer divisions leave orders 2, (5,6), (4,8), or (3,10). Coprime additive-period decomposition plus binary separability and density integrality show that the word is respectively 2, 5, 8/4, or 3 periodic. Direct residue-neighborhood checks give every solution and count. The aggregate 106 ceiling follows by disjoint sums. The standalone exact integer-polynomial verifier and exhaustive direct graph checks at n=7..18 reproduced the statements. Finite checks are corroboration, not the proof.

value.rationale: The 2026 existence classification leaves a natural, motivated enumeration problem: how many distinct regular sets realize each admissible parameter, and what are their forms? The unrestricted theorem gives all labelled sets for every one of 25 possible (a,b) pairs, shows binary Fourier rigidity to periods 2,3,5,8, distinguishes the 8|n and n=4(mod8) boundaries, and proves a sharp global cap of only 106 across arbitrarily large connected graphs, attained exactly when 120 divides n. This is stronger than recomputing known isolated efficient-code counts.
